ui.cfg_b_secrets: Where the GitHub token is read from
cfg.h.plugins.enabled: Off by default. Nothing of any plugin is loaded while it is off.
cfg.h.plugins.official.discussions.enabl: One search per hour for discussions of the watched repositories with no comment.
cfg.h.plugins.official.discussions.days: A discussion older than this with no comment is listed.
cfg.h.plugins.official.packages.enabled: Once a day. The token needs read:packages; without it the plugin says it could not look.
cfg.h.plugins.official.packages.max_vers: A package with more versions is listed. Nothing is deleted.
cfg.h.plugins.third_party.enabled: Only packages signed by a key of your keyring, always in a separate process. Signed does not mean safe: such a plugin can read your files, and on Windows and macOS it can use the network.
cfg.h.plugins.worker.timeout_s: A plugin of another person that does not finish in time is killed.
cfg.h.plugins.worker.max_output_kb: A plugin that says more is stopped.
cfg.h.plugins.worker.memory_mb: Applied with a Job Object on Windows and a resource limit on Linux; macOS may not apply it.
cfg.f.plugins.worker.platforms_ok: Systems where plugins of others may run
cfg.h.plugins.worker.platforms_ok: linux, windows, darwin. Empty: none. Where the network cannot be cut off the plugin is labelled "no network isolation".
cfg.f.plugins.official_timeout_s: Time limit of an official plugin (seconds)
cfg.h.plugins.official_timeout_s: Official plugins run inside the monitor in a thread of their own.
cfg.f.plugins.alert_title_max: Longest title of a plugin alert
cfg.h.plugins.alert_title_max: What a plugin says is untrusted: control characters are removed and the title is cut.
cfg.f.plugins.breaker.failures: Failures before a plugin is paused
cfg.h.plugins.breaker.failures: A paused plugin stays paused until you resume it.
cfg.h.plugins.reverify_on_start: A package whose key was revoked or whose file changed is paused. It is checked again before every run in any case.
cfg.f.plugins.entry_points: Find plugin packages installed with pip
cfg.h.plugins.entry_points: Only lists them: their code is never imported and each one is installed like any other, with its signature.
cfg.h.secrets.backend: local: as before. vault, sops, bitwarden, aws, azure, gcp: read only, with the login of that program; needs the stored token setting on.
cfg.f.secrets.reload_on_rotate: Read the token again now and then
cfg.h.secrets.reload_on_rotate: So that a rotated token is used without a restart.
cfg.f.secrets.reload_seconds: Seconds between two reads of the token
cfg.h.secrets.reload_seconds: If the read fails, the token read before is kept.
cfg.h.secrets.vault.addr: https://…; http only to this computer.
cfg.h.secrets.vault.path: The API path after /v1/, for example secret/data/monitor (KV version 2).
cfg.h.secrets.vault.field: The key inside the secret that holds the token.
cfg.f.secrets.vault.token_env: Vault: environment variable of its token
cfg.h.secrets.vault.token_env: The NAME of the variable, never the token itself.
cfg.h.secrets.sops.file: Decrypted with the sops program of this computer. Use it only on a computer you trust.
cfg.h.secrets.sops.field: The key of the file that holds the token.
cfg.h.secrets.bitwarden.item: Read with the bws program and its own BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN.
cfg.h.secrets.cloud.ref: aws: secret id; azure: secret identifier URL; gcp: secret name. Read with aws, az or gcloud.
egress.use.secrets_vault: Reads the GitHub token from your Vault
egress.fail.secrets_vault: The token read before stays; at start gh uses its own login
egress.use.secrets_tool: A secret manager program reads the GitHub token
egress.fail.secrets_tool: The token read before stays; at start gh uses its own login
cli.plugins.help: plugins: list, validate, pack, verify, init, install, enable, disable, uninstall, audit
cli.plugins.help_name: plugin: name of an installed plugin
cli.plugins.help_fingerprint: plugin install: fingerprint of the key, to confirm
cli.plugins.packed: Packed {package} (SHA-256 {sha}). Sign it with your own tools.
cli.plugins.confirm: Nothing was installed. To install it run again with --fingerprint {fingerprint}
cli.plugins.installed: {name} installed, switched off. Switch it on with plugin enable --name {name}
cli.plugins.official_setting: {name} is official: switch it off with its setting plugins.official.{name}.enabled
cli.plugins.made: Template of a plugin written in {folder}
ui.plugins.alert_discussion: {repo}: discussion #{number} without an answer for {days} days: {title}
ui.plugins.signed_not_safe: Signed does not mean safe: a signature says who made it, not what it does.
ui.plugins.title: Installed extensions
ui.plugins.uninstall_confirm: Remove the plugin {name} and its files?
ui.plugins.path_label: Signed package on this computer (.zip, with its .ed25519.sig next to it)
ui.plugins.install_confirm: Install {name} {version} by {author}? Permissions: {permissions}. Key fingerprint: {fingerprint}. Signed does not mean safe.
